summary.intent: Investigate and fix the flaky release_dry_run test in git_process_count_tests.rs (trail #357), which occasionally saw 10 git processes instead of 11, by finding the root cause and fixing it rather than widening the expected count.
summary.outcome: Root cause found and reproduced: the fixture repo's origin is a github.com URL, so `release --dry-run` runs ls-remote against it. With network, github.com answers 401 and git starts a credential helper (one extra process); offline or sandboxed, it does not. The fix rewrites the fixture origin to an empty local bare repo in crates/callisto-fixtures/src/perf.rs, which also covers the bench. The commit was being retried unsandboxed for signing, and the merge, push, PR and lead report were not done in this transcript.

repo: Process counts in git_process_count_tests are measured via GIT_TRACE2_EVENT, counting 'start' events.
The perf fixture repo's origin points at github.com, so any command that contacts the remote (e.g. release --dry-run's ls-remote) depends on network and credential-helper state.
crates/callisto-cli/benches/commands.rs also uses GIT_TRACE2_EVENT and the same fixture, so fixing the fixture covers both test and bench instead of patching each.
Fixture helpers such as callisto_fixtures::git::run_git exist for setting up repos in tests.

code.finding: Fixture generation now rewrites origin to an empty local bare repository, removing the network and credential-helper dependency from process counts (line numbers not given in the transcript).
Release flow code inspected to locate where git ls-remote is invoked against origin.

workflow: Temporarily tracing the git argv (an inspect/eprintln in the test) quickly showed which git processes release starts, and confirmed the 10 vs 11 difference (offline vs network).
Fixing at the shared fixture level was better than per-call-site env overrides (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/insteadOf), since it fixed the test and the bench together.
Review the staged diff before committing: a scripted/edit-tool change mangled a line and was caught and restored via git restore.
Commit signing needs gpg access outside the sandbox, so the signed commit has to be retried unsandboxed.
Follow the lead's rule of no session trailer: the first commit attempt included a Claude-Session trailer and was redone without it.
